articles.headline: India faces scrutiny over fraudulent e-waste recycling claims
articles.summary: India generated 1.41 million tonnes of e-waste in 2025-26, with informal operators handling 78% of the total. The Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework faces scrutiny over fraudulent certificates sold by recyclers. Only 18% of waste is currently captured by the formal and informal recycling systems. The government has ordered inspections of machines and mass-balance audits.

articles.headline: State revenue deficits rise as subsidy and cash transfer spending grows
articles.summary: The aggregate revenue deficit of Indian states rose to 0.7% of GDP in 2025-26, up from 0.2% in 2022-23. PRS Legislative Research reports that unconditional direct cash transfers now account for 1% of GDP. Rising power subsidies and rural employment guarantee outlays are narrowing fiscal space, potentially slowing capital expenditure and long-term economic growth prospects.

articles.headline: Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang would return if requested by board
articles.summary: Following his resignation, Nvidia founder Jensen Huang stated he would be honored to return as CEO if the board of directors determines it is in the best interest of shareholders and employees. Huang noted he has received significant support from employees and investors after stepping down from the leading artificial intelligence chipmaker.

articles.headline: India needs 22% growth in tourists to hit 10 million mark
articles.summary: Despite simplified visa rules, India faces a steep challenge to reach 10 million foreign tourist arrivals in 2026. Data through August shows weak growth, requiring a 21.6% year-on-year increase in the September-December period to reach the milestone. Arrivals in 2019 reached near 10 million before the pandemic hit the global travel sector.

articles.headline: Indian pharmaceutical exports to US drop 10% amid rising competition
articles.summary: India’s drug exports to the US fell nearly 10% to $9.47 billion in 2025-26 as generic competition and buyer consolidation eroded margins. Sales of the high-margin cancer drug Revlimid saw a significant decline following the end of volume curbs. Large drugmakers are shifting focus to complex products like biosimilars and peptides, which face less competition but require higher R&D costs.

articles.headline: Samsung Heavy Industries explores investment in Indian shipbuilding sector
articles.summary: South Korea’s Samsung Heavy Industries (SHI) is considering investing in Indian shipyards as its domestic facilities are fully booked for three years. SHI may expand its cooperation with Swan Defence and Heavy Industries (SDHI) at the Pipavav shipyard in Gujarat. The firm aims to use India as a base for overflow orders of large commercial vessels, including tankers and container ships.

articles.headline: Bosch in talks to sell portion of Indian IT operations
articles.summary: German auto parts maker Robert Bosch GmbH is in early discussions to sell parts of its Indian technology operations to contain costs. Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) is reportedly a suitor for the unit, which could involve transferring up to 3,000 employees. The move aligns with a trend of multinationals selling global capability centres (GCCs) to specialized Indian IT firms.

articles.headline: Nifty recovers losses from US-Iran conflict to hit pre-war levels
articles.summary: Indian equities became Asia's best performers this month as the Nifty 50 surpassed its pre-conflict high of 25,476 on Tuesday, closing at 25,387.40. Gains were driven by easing oil prices following US midterm election results and $10 billion in foreign inflows. Analysts suggest further room for growth due to better corporate earnings and an unwinding of global AI trades.

articles.headline: Tata trustees begin search for successor to N. Chandrasekaran
articles.summary: Tata Sons trustees, including vice-chairmen Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh, have agreed to begin the search for a successor to chairman N. Chandrasekaran. This follows Chandrasekaran's announcement that he will not seek a third term. Departing trustee Darius Khambata confirmed the timeline, noting that the selection committee process was discussed as early as August.

articles.headline: Gold loan NBFCs to seek RBI relief on capital norms
articles.summary: Gold-loan focused non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) are forming the Federation of Gold Loan Companies (FGLOC) to lobby the RBI for easier capital requirements and risk-weight norms. Lenders are concerned about asset quality and intensified regulatory inspections. Muthoot Finance executive vice-chairman George Alexander Muthoot called for smaller players to join for collective compliance.

articles.headline: Reducing emissions is an economic necessity, says Earthshot Prize chair
articles.summary: Jesper Brodin, chair of the Earthshot Prize, stated that adopting sustainable practices is a future-driven economic choice rather than a political one. He highlighted that even in hard-to-abate sectors like steel and cement, emission reduction strategies often prove economically more viable. Brodin noted that Ørsted reduced carbon emissions by 98% by rebuilding around renewable energy.

articles.headline: Government to scrutinize misleading front-of-pack product claims
articles.summary: The consumer affairs ministry plans to test trademarks and front-of-pack claims for food and cosmetics. Companies unable to substantiate claims like '100% whole wheat' or 'no added sugar' with credible evidence face delisting. The Central Consumer Protection Authority has already penalized firms for misleading descriptions on coconut water and bread packaging.

articles.headline: SEBI considers curbs on leveraged stock bets to manage volatility
articles.summary: The Securities and Exchange Board of India is weighing restrictions on new margin-funded stock purchases. Curbs may be triggered when leverage in a specific stock exceeds a threshold linked to its free float. The move comes as margin-funded bets reach record levels, raising concerns about potential market volatility.

articles.headline: Industry leaders seek tax incentives and expanded PLI schemes
articles.summary: Indian industry leaders have urged the government to widen Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes and offer targeted tax breaks for R&D. The goal is to raise manufacturing's share of the economy from 15% to 25%. Smaller businesses are also requesting cheaper credit and policy support to facilitate expansion.

articles.headline: Principal Secretary P.K. Mishra highlights India's governance journey
articles.summary: Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, P. K. Mishra, stated on Tuesday that India’s governance has been marked by defining milestones from vision to action. He emphasized that decisive leadership has been key to translating national goals into tangible outcomes during the country's development journey.

articles.headline: Microsoft launches Autopilot AI agent with human governance focus
articles.summary: Microsoft Corp. released 'Autopilot', an AI agent designed to automate enterprise tasks like procurement orders under strict human definitions. The launch follows a major outage of 365 business apps. Microsoft is emphasizing human control to address security and data leakage concerns that have slowed corporate adoption of AI 'agents'.

articles.headline: Redbrick Offices raises ₹530 crore in pre-IPO funding round
articles.summary: Managed workspace provider Redbrick Offices raised ₹530 crore in a funding round led by Abakkus Private Equity. The capital will be used to expand its 6.5 million sq. ft footprint to meet demand from global capability centres. Other participants included Evolvolence Equity Partners, IIFL Capital, and UTI Alternatives.

articles.headline: IITs return to offline recruitment tests to curb AI cheating
articles.summary: Recruiters at various IITs are shifting back to in-person hiring tests and interviews for the 2027 batch due to concerns over students using AI tools to cheat in online assessments. At newer IITs, firms opting for offline hiring rose to 70%. Recruiters want to ensure candidates possess genuine problem-solving skills without unauthorized AI assistance.

articles.headline: JLR performance weighs on Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles stock
articles.summary: Tata Motors shares dropped nearly 10% in two days as subsidiary Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) cut revenue and margin guidance for FY27. JLR expects an Ebit margin of 2-3% due to low China demand and supply chain issues. While the domestic India business grew 40% in volume, JLR’s slower recovery and delayed cash-flow breakeven point are worrying investors.

articles.headline: Kaynes Technology shares hit 52-week low after profit drop
articles.summary: Kaynes Technology shares fell 17% following a 62% year-on-year drop in Q2 net profit. High interest and depreciation from new projects, plus an 80% revenue fall in the smart meter segment, impacted results. The company has reduced meter supplies to prioritize recovering outstanding receivables from state governments.

articles.headline: Number of companies with 90% promoter pledging rises in Q2
articles.summary: BSE-listed companies with over 90% of promoter holdings pledged rose to 42 in the September quarter, up from 34 in Q1. High pledging levels alongside weak cash flows can signal financial stress. Promoters often borrow against shares for expansion or personal needs, but this increases vulnerability to forced selling during market corrections.

articles.headline: GIFT City to build regulatory framework for global commodity trade
articles.summary: The government has notified commodity trading contracts as financial products under the IFSCA Act, allowing GIFT City to regulate trades. The move aims to attract global commodity trading desks from hubs like Singapore and Dubai. Success will depend on framing detailed broking regulations and attracting specialist trade-finance banks to the IFSC.

articles.headline: Coal India explores IPOs for NCL and CCL subsidiaries
articles.summary: Coal India Ltd has begun preliminary talks for IPOs of its Northern Coalfields (NCL) and Central Coalfields (CCL) units next year. Each issue is expected to be ₹4,000-5,000 crore in size. The move follows government directives to list all Coal India subsidiaries by 2030 to improve transparency and unlock value for diversification into renewables and power.

articles.headline: US Polo Assn targets $4 billion global sales using India growth
articles.summary: US Polo Assn is targeting $4 billion in global business within eight years, with India as a primary driver. Indian sales are expected to reach ₹4,000 crore this year. Licensee Arvind Fashions plans to double the brand's store count to 1,000 outlets in the near future, integrating physical stores as fulfillment centers for digital and quick-commerce orders.

articles.headline: Nvidia India revenue comes mostly from software and support services
articles.summary: Nvidia’s Indian unit reported ₹7,361 crore in revenue last fiscal, with over 90% coming from software development and IT support for group companies. Unlike the US parent, the local entity books no chip product sales. Operating margins rose to 14.3%, even as Indian employees saw millions in paper wealth wiped out following CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and stock volatility.

articles.headline: Yes Bank AT-1 bondholders face further delay in interest payments
articles.summary: Axis Trustee Services has yet to issue a default notice to Yes Bank for a missed October interest payment on ₹5,450 crore of AT-1 bonds. Legal counsel stated that action is difficult until bonds are restored following a Supreme Court ruling. A review petition filed by the RBI has added further legal complexity for investors seeking their principal and coupons.

articles.headline: Listed hotel firms see Q2 revenue growth despite seasonal lull
articles.summary: IHCL, EIH, and Samhi Hotels reported healthy growth in the September quarter, driven by domestic leisure and corporate events. IHCL's revenue rose 22%, while ITC Hotels saw a 25.6% increase. Average occupancy rose 2 percentage points and room rates increased by 16%. Luxury hotels outperformed, benefiting from weekend staycations and a busy wedding season.

articles.headline: E-commerce firms upgrade AI tools to defend customer relationships
articles.summary: Amazon is upgrading its Rufus assistant and Flipkart is testing its SLAP tool to counter independent AI shopping agents that threaten to own product discovery. Agents like 'Flash' aim to facilitate orders and returns directly. Platforms are focusing on paid memberships and integrated credit cards to retain shoppers within their proprietary ecosystems.

articles.headline: Mars Pet Nutrition counts on scientific lead as FMCG rivals enter
articles.summary: Mars Inc. is defending its leadership in India's $2 billion potential pet food market against new entrants like Godrej Consumer and Reliance. Mars is focusing on localized products like Rohu fish and Chicken Biryani flavors. MD Manish Syag noted that while rivals have distribution, Mars' 20-year lead in scientific research and consumer trust remains a key differentiator.

articles.headline: BSNL losses widen to ₹1,532 crore in September quarter
articles.summary: State-owned BSNL's Q2 losses widened due to falling revenue from its fibre-to-the-home business and rising expenses from its 4G rollout. Total expenses rose 8.8% to ₹7,732.7 crore. Communications minister Jyotiraditya Scindia urged the operator to improve service levels and raise Arpu through household bundles to better compete with Reliance Jio and Airtel.

articles.headline: Crypto thieves hijack top websites including Zoom and CNN
articles.summary: Malicious JavaScript was found on 178 major websites, including those of Zoom, CNN, and IKEA, in an attempt to steal cryptocurrency. Researcher Scott Helme found the scripts aimed to replace payment addresses with attacker wallets and skim credit card numbers. The attack targeted visitors through Optimizely, a website optimization platform.

articles.headline: Vedanta expands hunt for critical minerals into potash and tungsten
articles.summary: Vedanta Ltd is moving into resources like potash, vanadium, and tungsten to meet India's demand for minerals that are difficult to process. The group entered India's first potash block to expand its fertilizer value chain. CEO Arun Misra stated the group plans to add several more minerals to its portfolio over the next five years, avoiding established metal markets.

articles.headline: Trump warns Iran of heavy price over alleged attack plot
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump stated that US authorities are investigating intelligence reports of an Iranian plot to target senior officials with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon. Trump warned Tehran would 'pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid' if the threats prove credible. The White House currently reports no immediate credible threat to the homeland.

articles.headline: Meta removes explicit Instagram content in India following scrutiny
articles.summary: Meta Platforms Inc. has removed more sexually suggestive and violent content from Instagram in India to comply with local recommendations. The company is using AI models to check content and reports that users now see unwanted recommended material half as often as a year ago. The move follows pressure from the Indian government regarding child safety and fair regulation.

articles.headline: BMW to roll out Alpina luxury brand in India in 2027
articles.summary: BMW plans to launch its Alpina brand as a standalone entity in 10 Indian cities next year. The German carmaker is recruiting for roles to select dealer partners and plan the rollout. The move targets wealthy buyers seeking customisation as top-end luxury car demand in India outpaces the overall auto market.

articles.headline: Shenzhen summit between Xi, Trump, and Putin worries global leaders
articles.summary: President Xi Jinping hosts Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen this week, sparking fears of a 'great power stitch-up'. While the leaders may discuss nuclear de-escalation and AI risks, European and Asian allies worry about being marginalized in regional conflict negotiations. Analysts expect the meeting to be more symbolic than a venue for major arms control deals.

articles.headline: US restricts advanced Nvidia AI chip exports to Southeast Asia
articles.summary: The US Commerce Department issued a rule requiring data centers in Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, and Brazil to obtain licenses for advanced AI chips. The measure seeks to block Chinese firms from accessing offshore computing power following an espionage scandal involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. The licenses will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis.

articles.headline: US chip export curbs put billions in Southeast Asian loans at risk
articles.summary: New US licensing rules for AI chips in Southeast Asia are forcing banks to re-evaluate billions in loans to regional data centers. Lenders fear losing critical Chinese offtakers like Alibaba and ByteDance. Some recent loan deals have already sought extra protections, such as mandatory repayment if customers are added to US restricted party lists.

articles.headline: Wall Street banks use hedge fund tactics to retain top traders
articles.summary: Banks like Citi and Jefferies are using breakup penalties, liquidated damages clauses, and immediate counter-offers to prevent senior traders from leaving for rivals. Citi recently wooed back its global exotics head after he nearly joined Barclays. The battle for talent in a limited pool has led banks to adopt more aggressive, restrictive employment contracts.

articles.headline: Inside the demanding workplace culture of Jensen Huang’s Nvidia
articles.summary: Former employees describe Nvidia as a 'family business' where Jensen Huang and his adult children, Madison and Spencer, wielded significant power without traditional hierarchy. While many praised Huang’s charisma and technical depth, others cited frequent public 'eviscerations' and a demanding environment. The disclosure of Huang's affairs ultimately led to his resignation.

articles.headline: Financial strategies for modern Indian households from DINKs to HENRYs
articles.summary: Changing family structures in India are driving new financial priorities. Child-free DINK couples focus on early term insurance and aggressive equity, while HENRYs (High Earners, Not Rich Yet) struggle with lifestyle inflation. Financial advisors recommend goal-based planning that accounts for life stages like maternity, career breaks, and pet care for 'Dinkwad' households.

articles.headline: Why cash flow is as critical as asset allocation for portfolios
articles.summary: Strategic asset allocation can fail if disconnected from cash flow needs. Investors are advised to match short-term commitments with liquid assets to avoid forced selling during market downturns. Net cash inflows offer a tax-efficient way to rebalance portfolios without incurring capital gains, ensuring equity compounding remains undisturbed during transitions.

articles.headline: AI tools promise to accelerate scientific research but require ethical frameworks
articles.summary: AI models like AlphaFold are transforming protein structure prediction and space data analysis. However, risks include a lack of transparency in 'black-box' methods and the potential for bio-warfare. Policies are needed to ensure scientific reproducibility and to prevent a widening R&D gap between wealthy nations and developing countries like India.

articles.headline: Extension of Agniver scheme should be used for better rehabilitation
articles.summary: The Cabinet's decision to extend the Agniveer service period to six years buys time but does not resolve long-term career uncertainty. Successful rehabilitation in the private sector or government posts is critical to maintaining the scheme's attractiveness. Every Agniveer should leave with a degree or a guaranteed job offer to ensure a sustainable 'second tour of duty'.

articles.headline: Traceability becomes a mandatory requirement for Indian food exports
articles.summary: Trade partners like the US and EU are increasingly making product traceability a condition for market access. India needs a public, government-led traceability system to help small and medium exporters track batch data across fragmented supply chains. Utilizing platforms like BharatTradeNet can reduce rejections and protect the reputation of Indian food brands.

articles.headline: Bunker Roy’s legacy highlights importance of grassroots skills in development
articles.summary: The passing of Bunker Roy, founder of Barefoot College, serves as a reminder that rural people hold significant tacit skills often overlooked by central planners. Roy’s model of training 'barefoot engineers' showed that development is most effective when it listens to those on the ground. Recognizing 'unskilled' work as highly specialized is key to inclusive growth.

articles.headline: India must practice deploying AI models at scale to remain competitive
articles.summary: As the US applies munition-style export controls to AI, India must focus on the ability to deploy large-scale models. History shows that technical knowledge eventually diffuses despite restrictions. By practicing deployment on independent infrastructure now, India will be ready to absorb and scale frontier AI technology when it inevitably arrives.

articles.headline: Poland's struggle shows difficulty of restoring institutions after populism
articles.summary: In Poland, Prime Minister Donald Tusk’s attempt to reverse the judicial captures of the previous right-wing government has led to a constitutional standoff. The crisis demonstrates that using 'militant' tactics to reclaim institutions can alienate voters. Repairing democratic stability requires radical change and credible, non-partisan restructuring rather than simple revenge.

articles.headline: ICC Reprimands Gurnoor Brar for Aggressive Send-off to Tim Seifert
articles.summary: India pacer Gurnoor Brar received an official reprimand and one demerit point from the ICC for using aggressive language during the fourth ODI against New Zealand. The incident involved a confrontational send-off to opener Tim Seifert, which the ICC deemed a violation of the Code of Conduct regarding demeaning celebrations that could provoke opposition players.

articles.headline: Karnataka Software Exports Account for Forty Percent of India Total
articles.summary: Chief Minister DK Shivakumar announced that Karnataka contributes $173 billion, or two out of every five dollars, to India's software and services exports. Speaking at the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit, he highlighted the state's attraction of $9.4 billion in FDI for the first half of FY 2025-26 and its growing status as a global hub for AI, deep tech, and semiconductors.

articles.headline: Russia Warns France Over Troop Deployment to Ukraine Conflict
articles.summary: The Russian government has stated it is aware of French troops being sent to Ukraine, characterizing the move as 'direct participation' in the ongoing war. This escalation follows reports of increased international military involvement, with Moscow warning that such actions significantly raise the risk of a broader conflict.

articles.headline: Lok Sabha Speaker Urges Women Legislators to Use AI Tools
articles.summary: Inaugurating the Commonwealth Women Parliamentarians India Region Conference in Bengaluru, Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla called on women MLAs and MPs to leverage artificial intelligence and digital platforms for better transparency. He emphasized that democracy strengthens when women hold leadership roles and shape policy across all levels of governance.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Orders Chhattisgarh to Pay Compensation for Illegal Detention
articles.summary: The Supreme Court directed the Chhattisgarh government to pay Rs 30 lakh to a man who spent over seven years in prison after his acquittal because the court order was not conveyed to jail authorities. The bench highlighted the state's failure to protect the man's liberty, noting that he lost his prime years due to institutional dysfunction.

articles.headline: Nine Killed as Bus Plunges into Gorge in Uttarakhand Tehri District
articles.summary: A bus traveling from Haridwar to Jyotirmath crashed through a barrier and fell into a gorge in Tehri district, killing nine people and injuring 25. Six passengers remain in critical condition at AIIMS-Rishikesh. Preliminary investigations suggest the driver failed to negotiate a sharp turn around 5 am on Tuesday.

articles.headline: Delhi Police Defend Jantar Mantar Protest Denial in Supreme Court
articles.summary: The Delhi Police Commissioner filed an affidavit in the Supreme Court stating that permission for a protest on Oct 10 was denied due to the Cockroach Janta Party's history of non-compliance and potential public order threats. The police argued that restrictive measures were necessary to prevent a dangerous situation in the national capital.

articles.headline: ASHA Workers Launch Indefinite Strike in Bengaluru Over Salary Delay
articles.summary: Over 40,000 ASHA workers gathered at Freedom Park demanding a fixed monthly pay of Rs 15,000 and the release of pending incentives promised in early 2025. Health Minister UT Khader met with the protesters and promised to discuss the honorarium issue with the Chief Minister, urging the workers to withdraw their strike.

articles.headline: Chandrayaan-3 Data Reveals Three Distinct Layers in Lunar Soil
articles.summary: Analysis from the Vikram lander's ChaSTE experiment has identified three layers within the top 10 cm of the Moon's surface at Shiv Shakti Point. Researchers found varying porosity and thermal properties, which could significantly impact future lunar habitat construction and efforts to explore water-ice in the Moon's southern high-latitude region.

articles.headline: Supreme Court Notice to Centre on All Assam Students Union NRC Plea
articles.summary: The Supreme Court has issued notices to the Centre and Assam government on a petition filed by the All Assam Students’ Union (Aasu) seeking a re-examination of the 2019 NRC. The union alleges that the final register contains significant errors and fails to accurately reflect the citizen count, seeking a fresh re-check to ensure an error-free list.

articles.headline: Lawrence Bishnoi Gang Labels Goldy Dhillon a Petty Criminal
articles.summary: Associates of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang have released a statement on social media dismissing Goldy Dhillon as a 'publicity-hungry petty thief'. The post, following Dhillon's threat against Amitabh Bachchan, prima facie confirms a split in the gang. The associates challenged Dhillon to a face-off and labeled him a police informer.

articles.headline: Quad Leaders Launch Military Maritime Patrol Exercise Scheduled for 2027
articles.summary: Leaders of India, the US, Japan, and Australia met in Manila for the Quad summit, committing to maritime patrol aircraft exercises in March 2027. The grouping expressed concern over economic coercion and emphasized the need for resilient supply chains. PM Modi proposed hosting the next summit in early 2027 to ensure regional stability.

articles.headline: Forensic Expert Claims Jeffrey Epstein Was Murdered in Jail
articles.summary: A forensic consultant who examined Jeffrey Epstein's full autopsy records has claimed the sex offender did not die by suicide but was murdered by strangulation. Dr. Michael Freeman noted that injuries to the neck and blunt force trauma found on the body were inconsistent with suicidal hanging, challenging the official determination by New York authorities.

articles.headline: Karnataka Sets November Deadline for Mekedatu Project Afforestation Land
articles.summary: The Karnataka government has directed officials to identify suitable land in three districts by the end of November for compensatory afforestation linked to the Mekedatu balancing reservoir project. The project requires over 5,000 hectares of forest land, and the state is racing to meet environmental clearance requirements to secure drinking water rights.

articles.headline: Medical Education in Kannada May Become Mandatory for RGUHS Courses
articles.summary: Rajiv Gandhi University of Health Sciences is considering making Kannada mandatory across all its programmes starting next academic year. Vice-chancellor BC Bhagavan stated that local language proficiency is crucial for effective patient-doctor interaction and that the university is currently assessing a pilot online learning programme.

articles.headline: Indian Seafarer Missing After Tanker Attack in Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary: An Indian seafarer is missing and two others are injured after the Panama-flagged LPG tanker MT TARA GAS was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz. The Ministry of External Affairs confirmed that 21 Indian crew members have been brought safely to Oman, while condemning the repeated targeting of commercial vessels in the region.

articles.headline: Bilkis Bano Vows to Fight Supreme Court Order Granting Bail
articles.summary: Bilkis Bano expressed shock after the Supreme Court granted bail to two convicts in her gang-rape case without giving her an opportunity to be heard. She stated that the order has reignited fears for her family's safety and that she will fight the decision to ensure justice for her children and other survivors.

articles.headline: Uttar Pradesh Draft Voter List Short of Adult Population Estimates
articles.summary: The draft electoral rolls for Uttar Pradesh show a total of 13.5 crore voters, which is 2.5 crore less than the state's projected adult population. Despite adding 18.8 lakh new names during a summary revision, the disparity remains high, particularly among women. Election officials have launched outreach programmes to identify eligible missing voters.

articles.headline: Study Finds Heavy Toll on Health of BMTC Women Conductors
articles.summary: A study by the University of Agricultural Sciences, Bengaluru, revealed that women conductors in the BMTC suffer from high body mass index and malnourishment due to erratic shifts and lack of restroom access. The research found that work pressure and home duties prevent them from maintaining nutritious diets, leading to chronic health issues and sleep deprivation.

articles.headline: Fifteen Year Wait Ends as Jakkur Railway Overbridge Opens Today
articles.summary: Chief Minister DK Shivakumar will inaugurate the 443-metre Jakkur railway overbridge, a project that was first initiated nearly 15 years ago. The four-lane bridge cost Rs 69.6 crore and is expected to save commuters 15 minutes of travel time toward Yelahanka and Ballari Road by bypassing the busy railway level crossing.

articles.headline: Alternative Tunnel Road Alignments Explored to Protect Lalbagh Garden
articles.summary: Bengaluru authorities are examining four alternative alignments for the proposed tunnel road to avoid building a launch shaft inside Lalbagh botanical garden. The changes could increase project costs by up to Rs 1,500 crore. The move follows strong public and environmental objections to using the historic garden for construction equipment.

articles.headline: Scrap Dealer Shot Dead in East Bengaluru During Altercation
articles.summary: A 45-year-old scrap dealer was found shot dead in his car in Manchappanahalli village on Tuesday morning. Police identified the victim as Imraz Pasha and suspect he was gunned down by a friend during a verbal dispute over monetary dealings. Investigators found three bullet wounds and are tracing a suspect who used a licensed pistol.

articles.headline: Bengaluru Man Dies After Being Slapped in Road Rage Dispute
articles.summary: A 40-year-old call centre employee died following a road-rage incident in Hennur when he was slapped by a man during an argument. The victim, William, had stopped his motorcycle to avoid hitting a child, leading to a heated exchange with the child's father. William collapsed after the physical assault and was declared dead at the hospital.

articles.headline: Unauthorised Drone Spotted Over Gorkha Rifles Military Mess Twice
articles.summary: Security concerns were raised in east Bengaluru after an unidentified civilian drone was spotted flying over the restricted Gorkha Rifles Officers’ Mess on Nov 12. Military officials filed a police complaint seeking an investigation into the person responsible for the flights, citing potential threats to safety and sensitive information leakage.

articles.headline: AI Tool for Preemie Eye Screening Receives Regulatory Approval
articles.summary: A homegrown AI tool designed to detect Retinopathy of Prematurity (ROP) in infants has received approval from the CDSCO. Developed by Remidio and KIDROP, the software analyzes retinal images at the bedside to flag suspected cases for specialists. The tool aims to prevent blindness in premature babies by bridging the gap in screening access.

articles.headline: Thief Disguised as Helper Steals Laptop from Injured Woman
articles.summary: A 39-year-old woman who fell off her scooter on a waterlogged stretch of Hennur Ring Road had her laptop bag stolen by a man pretending to help her. While bystanders assisted her after the crash, the suspect took advantage of the confusion to flee with a company laptop and valuables worth Rs 94,000. Police are investigating the incident.

articles.headline: Advocate Murder Accused Arrested in Bihar After Two Thousand Kilometer Ride
articles.summary: The prime suspect in the murder of a Whitefield advocate was apprehended in a remote Bihar village after traveling 2,000 km on a motorcycle to evade police. Amit Kumar Dubey rode across four states, surviving on roadside meals and avoiding public transport to bypass CCTV cameras. He was caught working as a farmhand using his grandmother's connections.

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate Accuses Former KPSC Chairperson of Multi Crore Scam
articles.summary: The ED has filed a prosecution complaint against former KPSC chairperson Shivashankarappa Sahukar and others for a recruitment scam involving veterinary officer posts. The agency alleges that the accused copy-pasted exam papers and correct answer keys for illegal gratification, amassing over Rs 4 crore in proceeds of crime.

articles.headline: Medical Students Allege Malpractice During Fellowship Exam at BMCRI
articles.summary: Medical postgraduates appearing for a fellowship exam at Bangalore Medical College and Research Institute have complained that an invigilator dictated answers to candidates. The students have demanded a fresh examination, citing a breach of integrity. RGUHS has requested CCTV footage and a report on the incident to determine further action.

articles.headline: Karnataka Government Employees Mandated to Declare Cash and Daily Movements
articles.summary: Starting Dec 1, all state government employees in Karnataka must declare the cash they carry and record their movements during office hours. The new rules, integrated into the AI-powered KAAMS system, aim to curb bribery and ensure staff availability during working hours. Failure to comply will lead to disciplinary action.

articles.headline: CM Clears Ten Thousand Crore Plan for Rural Road Connectivity
articles.summary: Chief Minister DK Shivakumar has approved a Rs 10,000 crore scheme to resurface 15,000 km of rural roads ahead of panchayat polls. The project focuses on upgrading damaged blacktop roads and enhancing major rural corridors. To ensure quality, contracts mandate GPS-tagged photographs and three separate inspections for every road project.

articles.headline: Samajwadi Party Likely to Offer Congress Only Twenty Four Seats
articles.summary: The Samajwadi Party is expected to offer Congress 24 out of 403 seats for the upcoming UP assembly elections based on a winnability criterion. While Congress initially sought parity and 181 seats, negotiations are expected to be tough. SP chief Akhilesh Yadav has reportedly shared a draft with Congress leadership focusing on past polling performance.

articles.headline: Nepal PM Shah Curtails India Visit to Twenty Five Hours
articles.summary: Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah has shortened his first bilateral visit to India to just 25 hours. He is seeking $2 billion in grants and loans for flood reconstruction and infrastructure projects. The visit will focus on economic cooperation and connectivity, though long-standing differences over hydropower and recruitment issues remain unresolved.

articles.headline: Meta Fine Tunes Instagram Recommendations for Safety in India
articles.summary: Meta has disclosed changes to Instagram's recommendation systems in India to reduce the visibility of sensitive content like violence and sexually suggestive posts. The move follows government advisories to review algorithms that suggest content to users. Meta stated that sensitive content reports have dropped significantly over the past year.

articles.headline: Two Dead in East Delhi Building Collapse Incident
articles.summary: A three-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man were killed after the roof of a house collapsed in east Delhi's Jwala Nagar. The 40-year-old building, constructed on encroached railway land, was poorly maintained. Police arrested the owner for culpable homicide, noting this is the sixth such fatal building collapse in the capital since September.

articles.headline: Amritpal Singh Granted Three Hour Parole for Grandmother's Last Rites
articles.summary: A court has granted Khadoor Sahib MP Amritpal Singh three hours of custodial parole on Nov 21 to attend his grandmother's cremation in Amritsar. Singh, who is currently lodged in an Assam jail, will be flown to Punjab under heavy police escort. The court also allowed him to join subsequent rituals via videoconferencing.

articles.headline: Allergy Pill Combinations Misused During Winter Pollution Surge
articles.summary: Health experts warn against the rampant overuse of montelukast-levocetirizine combination pills during winter smog in India. While these drugs provide relief from allergic rhinitis, they carry 'black box' warnings for serious neuropsychiatric side effects, including depression and suicidal thoughts, and should not replace prescribed inhaler therapies.

articles.headline: Study Identifies Five Distinct Subtypes of Type Two Diabetes
articles.summary: A new study in India has classified Type 2 diabetes and pre-diabetes into five subtypes based on insulin deficiency and resistance. The research found that South Asians are more prone to insulin-deficient subtypes, which carry higher cardiovascular risks. The findings suggest that current blood sugar tests may miss critical differences in disease progression.

articles.headline: US Polo Assn Aims to Double India Sales to Eight Thousand Crore
articles.summary: Apparel brand US Polo Assn expects its consumer sales in India to reach Rs 4,000 crore this fiscal year and plans to double that figure within five years. Growth strategies include opening 60-70 new stores annually, expanding into quick commerce, and focusing on premium products. India remains one of the brand's top three global markets.

articles.headline: Apple iPhone Shipments in India Drop Twenty Five Percent in Q2
articles.summary: iPhone shipments in India fell to 3.7 million units in the July-September quarter, a 25% drop compared to the previous year. Analysts attribute the decline to shortages of newer models and reduced discounts on older versions. Meanwhile, Samsung reclaimed the top spot in the Indian market as most other brands faced similar festive season slumps.

articles.headline: Amazon Invests Seven Billion Dollars in Indian Renewable Energy Projects
articles.summary: Amazon has committed an additional $7 billion to expand its renewable energy portfolio in India by 2030. The company announced four new utility-scale wind and solar projects with a total capacity of 934MW. The investment aims to support its global goal of reducing carbon intensity and powering its expanding data center operations in the country.

articles.headline: Sarvam AI Urges Affordable Pricing Models for Indian AI Adoption
articles.summary: Vivek Raghavan, co-founder of Sarvam AI, warned that India must build its own AI models and infrastructure to avoid becoming a 'digital colony'. Speaking at the Bengaluru Tech Summit, he called for AI inference priced in rupees per conversation rather than dollars per token, emphasizing that affordability is key to reaching a billion Indian users.

articles.headline: AI Models Misidentify Civilians as Military Targets in Simulation Tests
articles.summary: A research report by Vals revealed that advanced AI models from major tech firms frequently misidentify civilians, schools, and ambulances as military targets. In simulated scenarios, models like Claude Opus 5.5 regularly targeted non-military objectives, highlighting the risks of integrating unvetted AI systems into autonomous lethal weaponry.

articles.headline: Major Cyber Attack Targets One Hundred Seventy Eight Global Websites
articles.summary: A massive cyber attack has injected malicious code into websites of major organizations including the BBC, IKEA, and HSBC. The hackers used corrupted JavaScript to target tools hosted by Optimizely, seeking to steal financial information and infect Apple devices. Experts noted the attack was a coordinated attempt to exploit thousands of users online.

articles.headline: India Wins U20 SAFF Championship Title with Dramatic Late Goal
articles.summary: The Indian men's U-20 football team clinched their tenth SAFF Championship title after a 2-1 win over Pakistan in Dhaka. After a red card for Pakistan changed the momentum, India's Sandip Mandi scored a last-minute header to seal the victory. Coach Naushad Moosa praised the team's resilience despite injuries and missing key players.

articles.headline: Robert Pattinson Officially Cast as the Next James Bond
articles.summary: Robert Pattinson has been chosen to take over the role of James Bond, following Daniel Craig's departure from the franchise. The 40-year-old actor, known for his roles in Twilight and The Batman, becomes one of the few high-profile stars to lead the legendary spy series. Fans and critics have reacted with surprise to the meme-worthy casting choice.

articles.headline: Tamil Track Varuvaaiy Makes History with 2027 Grammy Nomination
articles.summary: The song Varuvaaiy, composed by Devan Ekambaram and featuring Susha, has become the first Tamil track to earn a Grammy nomination. Nominated in the Best Global Music Performance category, the track is a contemporary adaptation of a Bharathiyar poem. Devan highlighted the achievement for independent Indian musicians on the global stage.

articles.headline: Rupee Surges to Seven-Month High on Record Dollar Inflows
articles.summary: The Indian Rupee hit a seven-month high of 93.47 against the US dollar, defying a strong dollar index. Record dollar inflows in November, driven by foreign investors amidst retreating oil prices, bolstered the rupee's strength.

articles.headline: Amazon Plans $7 Billion Green Energy Investment in India by 2030
articles.summary: Amazon plans to invest $7 billion in renewable energy projects in India by 2030. This infusion will bolster its wind and solar energy portfolio, strengthen its position as a corporate buyer of carbon-free energy, and support local power needs.

articles.headline: Karnataka Pitches AI Hub and Robotics Zone in Tech Leap
articles.summary: Karnataka unveiled six innovation initiatives, including an AI Hub and a Robotics & AI Innovation Zone, positioning AI at the core of its growth. Bengaluru accounts for nearly 50% of India's AI and machine-learning talent.

articles.headline: SC to Decide on Rahul Gandhi's Questions to Election Commission
articles.summary: The Supreme Court will decide whether to allow Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders to serve interrogatories on the Election Commission of India (ECI). The ECI has filed objections, citing 'serious prejudice'.

articles.headline: US Plans to Curb China Chip Imports Despite Lobbying
articles.summary: The US plans to block Chinese data center equipment imports despite lobbying by tech giants. Concerns remain over China's dominance in optical transceivers and potential security risks.

articles.headline: Distinctive Colors Define Luxury Brands: Tiffany, Hermès, Valentino
articles.summary: Luxury brands like Tiffany (Blue), Hermès (Orange), and Valentino (Pink PP) build powerful identities through signature colours. These shades become visual identifiers, symbolising brand values and desirability.

articles.headline: Karnataka CM Defends Mekedatu Project, Asks TN Parties to Read SC Order
articles.summary: Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar defended the Mekedatu reservoir project, questioning if Tamil Nadu parties had read the Supreme Court order, which he stated clearly stipulated Karnataka's obligation to release water.

articles.headline: SSR Sees Voter Count Rise in Four Poll-bound States
articles.summary: Four poll-bound states reported an increase in voter numbers during the Special Summary Revision (SSR), with Uttar Pradesh adding 18.84 lakh voters. Punjab remained unchanged.

articles.headline: FPIs pump record $10 billion in November, highest monthly haul
articles.summary: Foreign portfolio investors purchased a record $10.07 billion worth of Indian equities in November. This surpasses the previous monthly record of $8.42 billion set in December 2020. The surge follows a global pivot towards emerging markets as US bond yields soften and the dollar weakens, marking a significant return of foreign capital to Indian markets.

articles.headline: RBI’s reply to Tata Sons triggers debate over suo motu powers
articles.summary: The RBI has directed Tata Sons to comply with all regulations governing Upper Layer NBFCs, including mandatory listing by September 2025. This response has sparked a legal debate over whether the regulator can compel a private firm to list its shares without specific statutory provisions. Legal experts suggest the directive could be challenged in court.

articles.headline: Govt working on standards for low-speed electric 2-wheelers
articles.summary: The Indian government is planning new regulations for low-speed electric two-wheelers to improve safety as e-commerce delivery fleets expand. Currently, these vehicles do not require a license or registration. New rules will focus on battery safety, vehicle identification, and performance standards to bring order to the unorganized market segment.

articles.headline: US curbs China’s remote access to AI chips after Nvidia scandal
articles.summary: The US has announced new rules to prevent Chinese firms from accessing advanced AI chips through remote cloud data centers in third countries. The move follows reports of Nvidia's hardware being accessed despite previous export bans. Beijing has slammed the restrictions as an abuse of export control measures that disrupts global supply chains.

articles.headline: Ashok Leyland greenfield capacity under consideration as utilization hits 90%
articles.summary: Ashok Leyland is considering setting up a new greenfield manufacturing plant as its current capacity utilization has reached 90%. The company expects strong growth in the medium and heavy commercial vehicle segment. Management is also monitoring commodity price inflation and may consider price hikes in the third quarter to protect margins.

articles.headline: Rane (Madras) targets strong growth in exports
articles.summary: Auto components maker Rane (Madras) expects strong double-digit growth in its export business, driven by new product launches and robust overseas demand. The company reported a total revenue of ₹1,242 crore in the first half of FY27. Management noted that domestic demand remains steady, supported by consumer sentiment and rising EV adoption.

articles.headline: ₹80,000 crore investment to make HZL largest zinc producer
articles.summary: Hindustan Zinc Plans to invest ₹80,000 crore over the next three to five years to double its production capacity to 2 million tonnes per annum. The expansion will cover the entire value chain from mining to finished metal. The company aims to become the world's largest zinc producer, holding nearly 15% of the global market share.

articles.headline: Trade restrictions spike in H1 even as facilitate measures rise: WTO
articles.summary: The WTO reported a sharp increase in new trade-restrictive measures by G20 economies in the first half of 2026, covering trade worth $2 trillion. However, trade-facilitating measures also rose, covering $1.3 trillion in imports. The WTO urged members to exercise restraint and maintain open, predictable trade to support global economic growth.

articles.headline: Quad leaders voice concerns over economic coercion at Manila meeting
articles.summary: Leaders from the US, India, Japan, and Australia expressed concerns over economic coercion and arbitrary export restrictions during a meeting in Manila. While not naming China, the leaders pledged to secure critical supply chains and promote a free and open Indo-Pacific. They also announced a new initiative to strengthen maritime domain awareness.

articles.headline: Rupee at 7-month high on FPI inflows and soft oil
articles.summary: The Indian rupee appreciated to a seven-month high of 93.5 against the US dollar, driven by record foreign portfolio investment inflows and lower global crude oil prices. This mark the second consecutive session of appreciation. Market participants believe the currency may remain strong if capital inflows continue and oil prices stay stable.

articles.headline: Piyush Goyal on two-day visit to Italy for trade ties
articles.summary: Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal is on a two-day visit to Italy to meet government leaders and business heads to boost trade and investment. He will co-chair the 23rd session of the India-Italy Joint Commission for Economic Cooperation. The visit aims to review the India-Italy Joint Strategic Action Plan 2025-29 and enhance bilateral cooperation.

articles.headline: ICAI President elected as board member of IFAC
articles.summary: Ranjeet Kumar Agarwal, President of the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI), has been elected as a board member of the International Federation of Accountants (IFAC) for a three-year term. He will represent India on the global accounting body, contributing to the development of international standards and the accounting profession.

articles.headline: Needless anxiety over SEBI plan for inactive demat accounts
articles.summary: SEBI's proposal to label demat accounts with no transactions for two years as 'inactive' has caused concern among investors. While aimed at preventing fraud, critics argue it may increase compliance burdens. Many inactive accounts belong to long-term investors or those with multiple brokerage accounts who do not frequently trade their holdings.

articles.headline: PLI scheme: Hits and misses after five years of implementation
articles.summary: A Niti Aayog assessment of the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme shows success in food processing and pharmaceuticals but policy gaps in solar PV and battery sectors. The scheme has helped reduce import dependency for certain key materials. However, challenges remain in achieving high value-addition and addressing supply chain bottlenecks.

articles.headline: Sagarinala blue bond issuance was a missed opportunity for green debt
articles.summary: Sagarinala Finance Corp's decision to scrap its planned blue bond issue is seen as a missed opportunity for India's nascent sustainable debt market. The ₹500-crore bond would have been a new asset class for investors interested in maritime and coastal infrastructure. High interest rate demands from investors led to the cancellation of the issue.

articles.headline: Neo-brokers lure investors but need better regulation, says report
articles.summary: Digital-first neo-brokers have fundamentally changed retail investing in India by simplifying account opening and reducing costs. However, a report highlights risks such as aggressive marketing and gamified interfaces that may lead to impulsive trading. Regulators are urged to increase oversight to protect inexperienced investors from operational and market risks.

articles.headline: Banking reform is long overdue to address MSME credit and security
articles.summary: Experts call for urgent banking reforms in India to improve credit access for MSMEs and strengthen cybersecurity. While the sector has seen a reduction in NPAs, challenges remain in the form of rising fraud and the need for higher interest rates to retain deposits. A committee has been tasked with creating a roadmap for these structural reforms.

articles.headline: SEBI may limit leveraged bets to curb market volatility
articles.summary: SEBI is considering limits on leveraged stock market bets through Margin Trading Facilities (MTF) to curb excessive volatility. The regulator is concerned about the rapid expansion of retail leverage, which could lead to sharp market corrections. Proposed rules may limit the amount of financing a broker can provide for a single stock.

articles.headline: Foreign outflows from India-focused offshore funds ease in Q3 2026
articles.summary: Net outflows from India-focused offshore funds and ETFs slowed to $3.9 billion in the quarter ended September 2026, down from $4.6 billion in the previous quarter. The decline is attributed to a correction in Indian equity valuations, which made them more attractive to long-term investors. However, offshore funds remain cautious due to global economic uncertainty.

articles.headline: Ashika PE raises ₹220 crore via new equity fund
articles.summary: Ashika Private Equity has raised ₹220 crore through its maiden fund, the Ashika Growth Equity Fund I. The fund will invest in 12-15 high-growth companies across various sectors. The firm aims to support businesses that have established business models and are looking for capital to scale their operations and reach the next level of growth.

articles.headline: BlackRock raises its stake in Axis Bank to 5%
articles.summary: Global investment giant BlackRock has increased its stake in Axis Bank to 5.01% through an open market purchase. The firm acquired over 18,000 shares, taking its total holding to more than 15.57 crore shares. Axis Bank recently reported an 18% increase in its second-quarter net profit, driven by strong growth in net interest income.

articles.headline: Ribbit Capital sells Groww shares worth ₹1,905 crore
articles.summary: US-based venture capital firm Ribbit Capital has sold shares of online brokerage platform Groww for ₹1,905 crore through block deals. The shares were purchased by a group of investors, including SBI Mutual Fund and Kotak Mahindra Mutual Fund. Ribbit Capital remains a significant shareholder in the company after the transaction.

articles.headline: Karnataka preparing to lead next phase of global innovation
articles.summary: CM DK Shivakumar announced that Karnataka is preparing for its next phase of growth by positioning itself as a global hub for deep-tech, biotech, and AI. Speaking at the Bengaluru Tech Summit, he highlighted the state's leadership in attracting FPI and its strong ecosystem for start-ups. The state aims to reach a GSDP of $1 trillion in the coming years.

articles.headline: Karnataka’s ₹390-crore deep-tech push relies on others for funding
articles.summary: Karnataka has committed ₹390 crore for three infrastructure projects at the Bengaluru Tech Summit, but this is only a small portion of the required ₹1,729 crore. The projects include a semiconductor fabrication facility and a deep-tech innovation hub. The state government is looking for contributions from the central government and private partners to bridge the gap.

articles.headline: India must build own AI infra to avoid ‘digital colony’ status
articles.summary: Industry experts at the Bengaluru Tech Summit warned that India must develop its own AI infrastructure and models to avoid becoming a 'digital colony'. They emphasized the need for data sovereignty and building AI systems that are tailored to Indian languages and cultural contexts. This will ensure that the country retains control over its digital future.

articles.headline: AI could expand India’s start-up market by making services affordable
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence has the potential to make financial, educational, and healthcare services affordable for millions of underserved Indians, according to industry leaders. AI-driven solutions can help start-ups reach new markets and improve the efficiency of their operations. This will create new opportunities for growth and innovation in the Indian start-up ecosystem.

articles.headline: AI will change how students learn, says National Testing Agency
articles.summary: AI is expected to transform the education system by moving beyond rote learning to test critical thinking and problem-solving skills. The National Testing Agency is exploring the use of AI to create more personalized and effective assessments. However, experts emphasized that foundational knowledge and human curiosity will remain essential for learning.

articles.headline: Memory will be critical to scaling AI as chip demand rises
articles.summary: As AI models grow in complexity, the performance of memory and storage will become increasingly important. Experts at the Bengaluru Tech Summit noted that fast and efficient memory is essential for processing large amounts of data. This will drive demand for high-bandwidth memory chips and other advanced storage solutions to support the next generation of AI.

articles.headline: Horticulture production rises 4% to record 386.92 mt in 2024-25
articles.summary: India's horticulture production is estimated to have risen by 4% to reach a record 386.92 million tonnes in the 2024-25 crop year. The increase is driven by higher output of fruits, vegetables, honey, and plantation crops. This record production will help ensure the country's nutritional security and provide a boost to the income of horticultural farmers.

articles.headline: Severe cyclonic storm Akvan triggers storm surge and heavy rain alert
articles.summary: The IMD has issued a red alert for coastal Andhra Pradesh and Odisha as Cyclone Akvan intensifies. Storm surges of up to 2 meters are expected to inundate low-lying areas. Heavy rainfall and wind speeds reaching 120 kmph are predicted to impact the region, leading to evacuations and emergency preparations by state authorities.

articles.headline: Black pepper prices hit new peak of ₹750/kg on supply woes
articles.summary: Black pepper prices have reached a new high of ₹750 per kg due to supply shortages and strong demand from masala manufacturers. Lower production in major growing regions and a delay in the onset of the new crop have contributed to the price rise. Traders expect prices to remain firm in the coming months as demand continues to outpace supply.

articles.headline: Centre urged to launch traditional rice mission in FY28 Budget
articles.summary: The Indian government has been urged to launch a National Traditional Rice Mission in the upcoming Budget to support the cultivation of indigenous rice varieties. These varieties are often more resilient to climate change and have higher nutritional value. The mission would provide financial and technical support to farmers to promote the growth of these varieties.

articles.headline: Farmwise combines AI with GIS to solve real-time farm problems
articles.summary: A new start-up, Farmwise, is using AI and geographic information systems (GIS) to help farmers solve real-time problems such as pest infestations and soil health issues. The platform provides farmers with personalized advice and recommendations to improve their crop yields and reduce their costs. This is an example of how technology can be used to support agriculture.

articles.headline: India moots stronger cooperation among coconut-producing nations
articles.summary: India has called for stronger cooperation among coconut-producing nations to address challenges such as climate change and falling prices. The move aims to promote the exchange of research and best practices to improve the productivity and sustainability of coconut farming. This will help support the livelihoods of millions of coconut farmers in India and other countries.

articles.headline: Apeda plans state-specific strategies to boost North-East agri exports
articles.summary: The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (Apeda) is developing state-specific strategies to boost agricultural exports from India's North-East region. The plans will focus on promoting unique products such as ginger, citrus fruits, and organic tea. This will help create new opportunities for farmers and exporters in the region.

articles.headline: Tech woes and higher rates drag copper to four-month low
articles.summary: Global copper prices have fallen to their lowest level in four months due to weakness in the technology sector and expectations of higher interest rates. The metal's price was also impacted by a stronger US dollar, which makes commodities more expensive for buyers using other currencies. Analysts expect prices to remain under pressure in the short term.

articles.headline: Crude oil slips as West Asian exports recover
articles.summary: Global crude oil prices fell on Tuesday as exports from West Asia recovered, easing concerns about supply disruptions. However, geopolitical tensions in the region and a weaker US dollar provided some support for prices. Market participants are monitoring the situation closely for any further developments that could impact the global oil market.

articles.headline: Industry bodies seek measures to stem FPI outflow, incentivize R&D
articles.summary: Major industry bodies have urged the government to take steps to stem the outflow of foreign portfolio investment and incentivize research and development. The recommendations include a graded scale of long-term capital gains tax and higher tax deductions for R&D spending. These measures are seen as essential for boosting economic growth and competitiveness.

articles.headline: ‘I consider myself responsible for 40% of country’s pollution’: Gadkari
articles.summary: Union Transport Minister Nitin Gadkari stated that he considers himself responsible for 40% of India's air pollution as the transport sector is a major contributor to emissions. He emphasized the need for the country to move towards cleaner fuels such as ethanol, hydrogen, and electricity. Gadkari also highlighted the role of the auto industry in reducing pollution.

articles.headline: Loan defaults up in consumer-facing segments, report shows
articles.summary: A report by CRIF High Mark indicates a rise in loan defaults in consumer-facing segments such as personal loans and credit cards. The increase is attributed to rising interest rates and higher living costs, which have put a strain on the finances of many borrowers. Lenders are urged to be more cautious and implement stricter credit appraisal processes.

articles.headline: DP World starts second Kochi and Colombo service
articles.summary: DP World has launched a second weekly service connecting Kochi and Colombo to enhance trade and logistics between India and Sri Lanka. The new service will provide more options for businesses and help reduce transit times. It is expected to boost the efficiency of supply chains and support the growth of maritime trade in the region.

articles.headline: Fresh snowfall draws tourists to Gulmarg, raising hopes for tourism
articles.summary: The first heavy snowfall of the season has drawn a large number of tourists to Gulmarg, raising hopes for a successful winter tourism season in Jammu and Kashmir. The snowfall has transformed the region into a winter wonderland, attracting visitors from across the country. Local businesses are preparing for a busy season as more tourists are expected to arrive.

articles.headline: Draft SAF policy to be released for public consultation, says Naidu
articles.summary: The Union Civil Aviation Minister, Kinjarapu Ram Mohan Naidu, announced that a draft policy on sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) will be released for public consultation soon. The policy aims to promote the use of SAF in the aviation industry and reduce its impact on the environment. The government is seeking input from stakeholders to ensure the policy is effective.

articles.headline: Instagram refines age guardrails after advisory from government
articles.summary: Instagram has announced new measures to improve its age guardrails and protect younger users from inappropriate content. The move follows an advisory from the Indian government and aims to ensure a safer online environment for children. The platform will use AI and other technologies to verify the age of its users and restrict access to certain content.

articles.headline: Air India, Airbus to study corporate SAF programme
articles.summary: Air India and Airbus have signed an agreement to study the feasibility of a corporate sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) programme in India. The study will explore the potential for using SAF in Air India's fleet and identify the challenges and opportunities for its adoption. This is part of the airline's commitment to reducing its environmental impact.

articles.headline: Extending EoM transition period to 3 years would make adjustment easier
articles.summary: In an interview, the CEO of IndiaFirst Life Insurance suggested that extending the transition period for the new Expenses of Management (EoM) regulations to three years would make it easier for insurers to adjust. The new rules aim to improve transparency and reduce costs for policyholders, but they also present challenges for the insurance industry.

articles.headline: Pragya Mishra to head OpenAI business for India and South Asia
articles.summary: OpenAI has appointed Pragya Mishra as its lead for business development in India and South Asia. Mishra, who previously worked for WhatsApp, will be responsible for building partnerships and expanding OpenAI's presence in the region. The move highlights the importance of the Indian market for the AI giant as it seeks to grow its business globally.

articles.headline: AI can distort climate information, warns UNESCO study
articles.summary: A study by UNESCO has warned that artificial intelligence can distort climate information and spread misinformation. The report highlights the need for greater transparency and accountability in the development and use of AI. It also calls for more research to understand the impact of AI on public perception and policy-making related to climate change.

articles.headline: India becoming an exporter of AI training without capturing value
articles.summary: A report suggests that India is becoming a major exporter of AI training services but is not capturing the full value of its contribution. The country provides a large pool of skilled workers for AI training, but most of the profits are being captured by foreign companies. The report calls for policies to support the development of a domestic AI industry.

articles.headline: US trade team discusses AI, data safety, IP with Indian officials.
articles.summary: US trade officials are meeting Indian bureaucrats to advance bilateral trade talks on IP, data protection, AI, and financial services. Discussions are ongoing, but not part of formal BTA negotiations. US highlights India's "Priority Watchlist" status for IP and concerns over insurance sector fairness.

articles.headline: Google discovers first autonomous AI cyberattack exploiting software flaws.
articles.summary: Google's GTIG and Mandiant found an AI-powered system, exploit_agent, that independently discovered and exploited software vulnerabilities without human intervention. The system automated reconnaissance, exploit generation, and post-intrusion actions, indicating a shift towards autonomous cyber operations.

articles.headline: Rupee posts strongest monthly gain in 20 months on foreign inflows.
articles.summary: The rupee gained 1.58% in November, its largest monthly rise since March 2025, closing at 93.47 against the dollar. This recovery is driven by $6-7 billion in foreign portfolio inflows and a decline in crude oil prices, stabilizing after recent geopolitical tensions.

articles.headline: Sebi considers tightening rules for margin trading facility.
articles.summary: Sebi may tighten MTF regulations following industry feedback on its ~1.46 trillion growth. Proposals include market-wide position limits similar to derivatives, based on ADTV or free-float, and excluding surveillance stocks.

articles.headline: Aether Industries signs supply agreement with Baker Petrolite.
articles.summary: Aether Industries has entered into a facility development and supply agreement with Baker Petrolite. The company's stock closed 1.7% up.

articles.headline: USFDA classifies Caplin Point steriles facility as OAI after inspection.
articles.summary: The USFDA has classified Caplin Point Laboratories' sterile facility in Gummidipoondi as Official Action Indicated (OAI) following an inspection. The stock closed 4.0% down.

articles.headline: Sigma Advanced Systems forms JV with Spain's EM&E for defence.
articles.summary: Sigma Advanced Systems announced a strategic joint venture with Spain’s EM&E group to enhance indigenous defense manufacturing. The company's stock closed 5.0% up.

articles.headline: IndusInd Bank partners Mastercard to boost Asia-Pacific outbound payments.
articles.summary: IndusInd Bank has collaborated with Mastercard to enhance outbound cross-border payments from India across the Asia-Pacific region. The bank's stock closed 2.0% up.

articles.headline: TCPL Packaging enters JV with Brandart to explore packaging business.
articles.summary: TCPL Packaging has entered a joint venture with Italian firm Brandart to explore the packaging business across Asia-Pacific. The company's stock closed 2.6% up.

articles.headline: UltraTech Cement challenges CCI cartel probe in Supreme Court.
articles.summary: UltraTech Cement has moved the Supreme Court, challenging a Delhi High Court judgment that upheld CCI's decision to allow the Builders Association of India to participate in an alleged cartelisation and price manipulation probe.

articles.headline: Foreign AI risks making India a digital colony, warns Sarvam cofounder.
articles.summary: Vivek Raghavan, cofounder of Sarvam AI, warns India risks becoming a "digital colony" by relying on foreign AI models, exporting data, and importing intelligence. He advocates building sovereign models, emphasizing Indic languages and voice AI for true digital equality.

articles.headline: AI can drastically cut drug development time to 1-2 years.
articles.summary: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw of Biocon stated at Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026 that AI has the potential to reduce drug development timelines from 5-7 years to just 1-2 years, accelerating precision medicine and addressing global health challenges.

articles.headline: Baidu CEO warns AI bubble looms without profit generation.
articles.summary: Baidu CEO Robi Li cautioned that heavy AI investment must generate significant revenue and profit, or concerns about an AI bubble could become reality. He noted most firms are yet to see substantial gains from AI spending.

articles.headline: Microsoft bug caused global outage, undetected since July.
articles.summary: A bug present since July crippled Microsoft's productivity software on November 11 for 15 hours. Routine user traffic rerouting, combined with prior server capacity loss, triggered failures across Teams, Outlook, and Copilot, embarrassing the tech giant.

articles.headline: Karnataka aims to be global hub for AI, deep tech, and semiconductors.
articles.summary: CM D K Shivakumar announced Karnataka's ambition to lead in AI, deep tech, and semiconductor manufacturing, backed by progressive policies, research, and a thriving startup ecosystem. The state accounts for 40% of India's software and services exports.

articles.headline: US financial tech firm SEI opens Global Capability Centre in Hyderabad.
articles.summary: US-based financial technology firm SEI launched its Global Capability Centre in Hyderabad, scaling operations with 800 professionals and capacity for 1,200. Hyderabad has attracted 150 new GCCs in 30 months, creating over 750,000 jobs.

articles.headline: India's IT spending expected to hit ₹16.9 trillion in 2027.
articles.summary: Gartner forecasts India's IT spending to increase by 10% to ₹16.9 trillion in 2027, driven by GCC expansion, AI-optimized infrastructure, cloud services, cybersecurity, and data modernization. IaaS is projected for the highest growth at 40.3%.

articles.headline: Indian steelmakers warn of high costs, China import threat, seek reforms.
articles.summary: Top Indian steelmakers are concerned about high production costs, raw material access, and potential Chinese steel imports. They urge mining and tax reforms, better logistics, and increased domestic raw material availability to enhance global competitiveness.

articles.headline: Ashok Leyland finds loan discrepancies at merger-bound Hinduja Leyland Finance.
articles.summary: Ashok Leyland discovered discrepancies in loan balances and transactions at its financing arm, Hinduja Leyland Finance (HLF), ahead of its merger into NDL Ventures by Q4FY27. An independent agency is conducting a comprehensive review.

articles.headline: Shipbuilders seek demand clarity and concessions for India investments.
articles.summary: Global shipbuilders, courted by India, request greater visibility of domestic demand and key concessions. HD KSOE's $4 billion investment for a Tuticorin facility relies on resolving concerns about steel supply consistency and domestic content norms.

articles.headline: India, Egypt form working group for trade agreement discussions.
articles.summary: India and Egypt agreed to establish a working group to discuss modalities for a preferential trade agreement (PTA/FTA) or comprehensive economic partnership agreement (CEPA). This follows Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal's visit, reaffirming bilateral commitment.

articles.headline: Industry seeks manufacturing finance, MSME support in Union Budget.
articles.summary: Industry bodies, including Ficci and Assocham, proposed a dedicated DFI for manufacturing, PLI for advanced battery components and robotics, and a National Enterprise Graduation Mission for MSMEs in pre-Budget consultations with FM Sitharaman.

articles.headline: BPCL plans ~9,000 crore bond issue after four years.
articles.summary: State-run Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) plans to raise around ₹9,000 crore through local corporate debt, targeting a five-year tenor, to fund capital expenditure. Discussions with bankers are underway, with issuance expected by December.

articles.headline: Government increases windfall gains tax on diesel, ATF exports.
articles.summary: The government hiked the windfall gains tax on diesel exports to ₹14/litre and ATF exports to ₹12.5/litre for the fortnight starting November 16, while retaining the zero levy on petrol.

articles.headline: GST return changes proposed to reduce errors and improve compliance.
articles.summary: Businesses may see fewer GST notices and clearer input-tax credit claims from April next year due to proposed changes. These require correcting errors in GSTR-1/1A instead of summary returns and formally recognizing online facilities like the Invoice Management System.

articles.headline: Panama-flagged tanker targeted in Hormuz Strait; 24 Indians safe.
articles.summary: Panama-flagged LPG tanker TARA GAS was targeted in the Strait of Hormuz on November 16. Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal confirmed 24 Indian nationals are safe, but one Indian seafarer remains missing.

articles.headline: States’ fiscal deficit projected to narrow to 2.9% in FY27.
articles.summary: States' combined fiscal deficit, excluding Central interest-free loans, is budgeted to narrow to 2.9% of GDP in FY27 from 3.4% in FY26. However, nine states are projected to exceed the 16th Finance Commission's 3% limit.

articles.headline: Yamuna's BOD levels in Delhi 10x safe limit during Chhath Puja.
articles.summary: Biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) levels in the Yamuna River in Delhi reached 30 mg/litre during Chhath Puja, ten times the safe limit. The Supreme Court warned states and UTs in the Yamuna basin of penalties for deteriorating water quality.

articles.headline: PM Modi launches seafarers' safety initiative at East Asia Summit.
articles.summary: PM Narendra Modi announced a seafarers' safety initiative at the EAS in Manila, boosting joint training and emergency response. He also highlighted increasing pressure from conflicts on food, fuel, and fertilizer supplies and discussed cooperation in civil nuclear energy and maritime security.

articles.headline: Government prepares chickpea contingency plan as sowing lags.
articles.summary: The government prepared a contingency plan for chickpeas as sowing lags in major states due to drought and low rainfall. Sowing is 21.9% lower than last year, prompting agronomic advisories to prevent crop losses.

articles.headline: Scaling up CBG can save India $20 billion in LNG imports by 2030.
articles.summary: A CII and EY-Parthenon report suggests India's 472 mt annual feedstock could support 62 mtpa of compressed biogas (CBG), potentially substituting $20.6 billion in LNG imports by 2030. Policy support, financing, and off-take visibility are crucial.

articles.headline: Next governance phase must prioritize citizen experience: P K Mishra.
articles.summary: P K Mishra, Principal Secretary to the PM, stated that the next phase of Indian governance should focus on how services are delivered to citizens, emphasizing being heard, receiving real-time decisions, and being treated with dignity, rather than just program numbers.

articles.headline: Grand Theft Auto VI launch sparks feverish global anticipation.
articles.summary: Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto VI, after 13 years, launches Thursday to immense anticipation, with millions pre-ordered and fans rearranging lives. With an estimated $1 billion budget, it's one of gaming's most expensive titles, crucial for Take-Two Interactive.

articles.headline: Nvidia faces scrutiny amid CEO's resignation, US export curbs.
articles.summary: Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang resigned over alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, wiping over $400 billion off market value. The Trump administration simultaneously imposed further restrictions on China's access to Nvidia's advanced AI chips.

articles.headline: Indian markets rally for second day on foreign fund inflows.
articles.summary: Benchmark indices extended gains for a second consecutive day, with Sensex up 427.40 points and Nifty at 25,387.40. Steady foreign fund inflows, moderate crude oil prices, and buying in Reliance Industries and bank stocks drove the rally.

articles.headline: Stock brokers propose STT and LTCG tax relief in Budget.
